Freeze a SAS-built dataset as a checksummed parquet oracle

Source: R/snapshot_oracle.R
snapshot_oracle.Rd

Reads a SAS dataset once with haven, writes it as parquet, and returns a record of what was written including a SHA-256 checksum of the parquet file.

Usage

snapshot_oracle(sas_path, out_path, expect = NULL, manifest = NULL)

Arguments

sas_path

Path to the SAS dataset (.sas7bdat).

out_path

Path to write the parquet file. Must not already exist.

expect

Optional named list validating the conversion, with any of n_rows, n_cols, and variables. Supply values read from SAS-side PROC CONTENTS. A mismatch is an error.

manifest

Optional path to a manifest YAML. When supplied, the snapshot is recorded with hvtiRutilities::update_manifest() so that hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest() can later detect a drifted oracle.

Value

Invisibly, a list with elements path, n_rows, n_cols, variables, and sha256.

Details

The snapshot exists so that equivalence testing has a fixed reference. A SAS-built dataset on a shared volume can be regenerated at any time; if it changes mid-migration, every previously passing comparison silently becomes meaningless. A checksummed snapshot is a citable fixed point.

Note that this does not remove haven from the chain of custody — it confines it to a single audited step. A misread is faithfully preserved in the parquet file. Supply expect to validate the conversion against SAS-side PROC CONTENTS output.

See also

compare_built()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  src <- system.file("extdata", "oracle_small.sas7bdat",
                     package = "hvtiRdatasets")
  snapshot_oracle(src, tempfile(fileext = ".parquet"))
}
# }
